test_command: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.UnitTests/Biolog.UnitTests.csproj && dotnet test tests/features/bio-trn-003/Biolog.Features.TransportNotifications.Tests.csproj && bash scripts/check-module-project-references.sh && python3 scripts/check-traceability.py --all && bash scripts/secret-scan.sh && (cd web && npx tsc --noEmit) && (cd tests/frontend && npx vitest run) && (cd tests/frontend && npx playwright test bio-trn-003-transport-notifications)
notes:
Seyi's first-pass review (SY-TRN003-01, High): InMemoryTransportNotificationRuleRepository.UpdateAsync was a blind dictionary assignment with no atomicity between TransportNotificationRuleService.SetEnabledAsync's own version check and its write - two concurrent callers racing from the SAME stale read could both pass the version check, both compute their own 'version + 1', and both write, the second silently clobbering the first instead of being rejected. Seyi's own deterministic reviewer probe (evidence/features/bio-trn-003/codex, commit 6f3cf6f) demonstrated this concretely.

Fixed by replacing ITransportNotificationRuleRepository.UpdateAsync with TryReplaceAsync(expectedCurrent, updated), backed by ConcurrentDictionary<TKey,TValue>.TryUpdate - the BCL's own atomic compare-and-swap, which only commits when the stored value still equals expectedCurrent at that exact instant. SetEnabledAsync now re-reads and throws RuleConcurrencyConflictException with the real current version when it loses that race, instead of silently losing a write - the identical 'ownership via identity, never content inspection' discipline this session's IIdempotencyStore.Claim/IWebhookDeliveryAuditSink.TryRecordOnceAsync already established, applied here to a record REPLACE rather than a create. Full reasoning (including why relying on record equality is safe specifically because GetAsync always returns the dictionary's own live reference) is in TryReplaceAsync's own doc comment and docs/features/bio-trn-003/README.md's own 'SY-TRN003-01 fix' section.

Seyi's own SeyiRuleConcurrencyProbe.cs was adapted (not deleted or ignored) to the new TryReplaceAsync interface shape - her own read-gating coordination strategy (both callers' GetAsync blocks until both have read the identical stale snapshot before either is released) is preserved unchanged; only the write-side method signature and the test's own exception-tolerance (the fix means the loser now THROWS RuleConcurrencyConflictException, which her original bare Task.WhenAll would have let propagate uncaught) were updated. A second, independently-authored barrier-gated test (Two_genuinely_concurrent_toggles_from_the_same_stale_read_commit_exactly_once) gates TryReplaceAsync itself via a System.Threading.Barrier(2) and asserts exactly one of two racing toggles commits while the other is rejected as a conflict, with the stored record ending at version 2 either way.

Also flagged to god as an FYI (not fixed here, out of this story's own owned paths): BIO-INT-004's own already-accepted InMemoryWebhookSubscriptionRepository.UpdateAsync has the identical blind-assignment shape.

This is a web-only-untouched, backend-only fix - no .tsx/.ts files changed, so tsc/vitest/Playwright were not re-run (unaffected by this remediation; their last-captured outputs from the first builder pass remain valid and are not overwritten here).

Verified: dotnet build clean. 248/248 integration, no regression. 210/210 unit, no regression. 21/21 feature-unit tests (19 original + Seyi's own adapted probe + 1 new independently-authored concurrency test), re-run 3x to confirm the two concurrency tests are not flaky - all three runs clean. Module-reference/secret-scan/traceability all PASS.
